target_customer: Companies, especially tech and fintech firms, sending or receiving cross border payments with a focus on Latin America
problem: Moving money across borders is slow and costly, and compliance is complex. BlindPay offers one API that connects fiat, stablecoins, blockchains and local rails such as Pix, SPEI and PSE with compliance handled.

founders.name: Bernardo Simonassi
founders.background_notes: At PicPay he worked on instant payment solutions for 60M+ users, per the YC page.

founders.name: Joao Borges
previous_startups: A large Brazilian blockchain startup (seven digit revenue in year one, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Nouns DAO contributor and Forbes 30 Under 30 per YC page.

founders.name: Gabriel Lyra
founders.role: CTO (named in launch post, not in YC founder list)
founders.background_notes: One aggregator reports he left in May 2026; not confirmed by a primary source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating local rails across several countries and stablecoin chains is standard engineering but compliance and banking partnerships are the hard parts for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Licences, local rail connections and banking partners take time to build and customers integrate the API, but larger players can offer similar orchestration.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later comparison guides describe Bridge as part of Stripe and BVNK as joining Mastercard, so well funded players occupy the wedge; BlindPay stayed independent through late 2026 in the sources found.

market_need_then: Stablecoin payments were growing fast and Latin American companies needed local currency access. The company reported $900,000 in total payment volume in 2024, according to a Brazilian outlet.

identity.visual_style: Developer focused API site with docs, MCP server and agent skills

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage is about funding and product, with no source on brand recall; the name is easy to say but resembles other products.

outcome_analysis: BlindPay is active and growing in the sources found. It raised a $3.3M seed in August 2025 from YC, 468 Capital, Circle Ventures, Bitso Business and angels, and has kept shipping through 2026 with new rails and banking partners. The tailwind is stablecoin adoption and Brazilian fintech experience in the founding team, while the risk is heavy competition from better funded orchestration providers.
notes: Aggregators report a separate $500K pre-seed in March 2025 (total $3.8M); this is unverified and not recorded as a round. Investor lists differ between the company blog and trade press (Transpose Platform, Acacia Venture Capital Partners, Kulveer Taggar appear only in press or aggregators). Announcement date varies from 2025-08-01 to 2025-08-08. No dated competitor sources from the 2025 batch period were found, so the list is empty; the competitor search returned only 2026 guides. CTO departure and Brazil VASP status come from one aggregator and are unverified.
